title: Half of humanity
hook: There are about two hundred countries. How few hold half of all people?

knows: that China and India are very populous
roughly where the large countries are on a world map
doesNotKnow: how few countries make up half the world's people
that land area and population are very different maps

misconception: People are spread roughly evenly across the countries, so "half the world" means dozens of countries.
objective: The learner can say that the seven most populous countries hold about half of humanity, and that a map of land area does not show where people are.

claims.text: Populations in mid-2024 (millions): India 1,451, China 1,419, USA 345, Indonesia 283, Pakistan 251, Nigeria 233, Brazil 212, Bangladesh 174, Russia 145, Ethiopia 132, Mexico 131, Japan 124, Egypt 117, Philippines 116, DR Congo 109; world 8,162.
claims.source: UN DESA, World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant, total population as of 1 July 2024 (population.un.org/wpp). The figures in Demo.tsx agree with the brief to the million but were entered from the builder's recall: the builder could not open the UN portal (network blocked, 403). A fact-checker must compare every value with the WPP 2024 table. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (left unverified): Checker could not reach the UN WPP portal either (egress blocked: population.un.org, data.un.org, Wikipedia, OWID all 403). Partial corroboration only: populationpyramids (UN WPP 2024 based) lists India 1,450,935,802 and China 1.42 billion; INED's WPP 2024 table gives 2025 values (Nigeria 238, Brazil 213, Bangladesh 176, Russia 144, Ethiopia 135, Mexico 132 million) consistent with the 2024 values here given 1-2% growth; world 8.2 billion confirmed. The lesson conclusion (seven countries, 51.4%) is robust to these ranges, but every value still needs a direct compare with the WPP 2024 table by someone with access. Demo.tsx has Japan 123.75 vs the claim's rounded 124 (fine). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Pass 4: egress still blocked (population.un.org, data.un.org, ourworldindata.org, api.worldbank.org all 403 via proxy). Only new corroboration: UN WPP 2024 world total for 2024 = 8,161,972,573 (Iberdrola-hosted extract of the WPP 2024 regional tables) matches 'world 8,162'. Country values still need a direct compare with the WPP 2024 table. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 5): population.un.org still unreachable (page fetch fails at DNS; web search only returns aggregators). Corroboration only, not a direct compare: populationpyramids (WPP 2024-based) lists Indonesia 283.5M, Pakistan 251.3M, Nigeria 232.7M, Brazil 212.0M, US 345.4M, India 1,450,935,802; consistent with this list. Left unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): population.un.org still unreachable (proxy returns 403 on CONNECT). No direct compare possible; left unverified. Needs someone with access to the WPP 2024 table. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Pass 9: population.un.org still unreachable (proxy CONNECT 403). No direct compare with the WPP 2024 table possible; left unverified. Needs a human source check (founder or anyone with access). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Compared with WPP 2024 data files from the wpp2024 R package (github.com/PPgp/wpp2024, data from the UN Population Division; population.un.org still blocked). Mid-2024 rebuilt three ways from data/miscproj1dt.rda and popproj1dt.rda: births/CBR, deaths/CDR, and the mean of 1 Jan 2024 and 1 Jan 2025. All 16 values round to the claim: India 1,450.9, China 1,419.3, USA 345.4, Indonesia 283.5, Pakistan 251.3, Nigeria 232.7, Brazil 212.0, Bangladesh 173.6, Russia 144.8, Ethiopia 132.1, Mexico 130.9, Japan 123.75, Egypt 116.5, Philippines 115.8, DR Congo 109.3, world 8,161.97. The mean matches Demo.tsx to 0.01 M. These are also the 15 largest (Viet Nam 16th, 101.0). Not a compare against the portal's own July-1 table, but the data are the UN's own WPP 2024 release.

claims.text: The seven most populous countries hold about 51.4% of humanity; the first six hold 48.8%.
claims.source: Cumulative sums of c1 over 8,161.97 million: 6 countries 3,983.13 (48.80%), 7 countries 4,195.12 (51.40%) (artifacts/scratch/w1-pop.mjs). The margin is small, so the order of Indonesia, Pakistan and Nigeria is not claimed beyond c1. | Builder (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H, v3): reveal paragraph 1 changed: when the learner adds the seven largest in order it now reads 'India, China, the USA, Indonesia, Pakistan, Nigeria and Brazil: your Seen line shows the seventh took the bar from 48.8% to 51.4% of the world's 8.2 billion people (UN, 2024).' (both values recorded at the crossing); otherwise 'hold 51.4% ...; the first six only 48.8%.' plus the learner's own crossing. Reopened: unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Read v3 Demo.tsx first. Own node sum of POP (UN WPP 2024 values as in Demo.tsx) over WORLD_M = 8161.97: cumulative 17.78, 35.17, 39.40, 42.87, 45.95, 48.80, 51.40%, so the first six give 48.8% and the seven give 51.4%. ppl() prints one decimal. The values themselves rest on the UN figures (covered by the lesson's other claims); this claim is the arithmetic.

claims.text: There are about two hundred countries.
claims.source: 193 UN member states plus 2 observer states (UN). WPP itself reports 237 countries and areas. 'About two hundred' is a rounding of 195.

claims.text: Equal Earth is an equal-area projection, so drawn size is real size.
claims.source: Savric, Patterson and Jenny (2018), The Equal Earth map projection, IJGIS 33(3): 454-465. | Builder (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H, v3): reveal wording changed to 'On this equal-area map, drawn size is real size:'; the stage footnote 'Equal-area map. ...' now hides when the reveal opens, and the map stays on screen at the reveal (66% of natural height). Reopened: unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Checked as a property of the map drawn, not from Šavrič et al. (not opened). Own run of d3-geo 3.1.1 geoEqualEarth().fitSize([320,156], Sphere): planar area / spherical area for 116 countries (geoArea > 0.002 sr) is 3489 to 3511, a 0.64% spread; 10° cells at latitudes −80 to 80 give 3482 to 3506. That is constant up to edge resampling. As a control, Mercator gives 23,574 at the equator vs 133,371 at 60°. So drawn area is proportional to real area on this stage.

claims.text: Those seven countries cover about 25% of the land outside Antarctica.
claims.source: geoArea of the seven 1:110m country shapes over the sum for all countries except Antarctica: 34.2M / 135.0M km2 = 25.3% (w1-pop.mjs). 1:110m shapes are generalised; the share moves by well under a point at finer resolution (not checked). | Builder (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H, v3): reveal sentence changed to 'your 7 cover 25% of the land outside Antarctica, yet hold half of everyone.' The three readout tiles are now one status line '<n> countries · <x>% of people · land outside Antarctica <y>%'. Reopened: unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own run with the lesson's own shapes (kit/geo countries-110m.json via topojson-client, d3 geoArea): the 7 countries / all countries except Antarctica = 25.33%, which lnd() prints as '25%'. This matches the reveal fallback '25%' and the crossed.land recorded when half is crossed in order. At 1:110m resolution it is 'about', as the claim says.

claims.text: Russia adds about 13 points to the share of land outside Antarctica but under 2 points to the share of humanity.
claims.source: People: 144.82 / 8,161.97 = 1.77% (UN WPP 2024, c1). Land: geoArea of the 1:110m Russia shape over the non-Antarctic land total, computed in Demo.tsx; the r6 walkthrough shows the land readout going 25% -> 38% and people 53.5% -> 55.3% when Russia is added ninth (company/reviews/half-of-humanity/2026-10-14-learner-big-country-knower-r6.md). The reveal quotes the learner's own recorded before/after readouts, so the exact figures depend on what was already selected; only the size of the jump is claimed. Not checked outside the page. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own node (fc26-b0/half.mjs, d3 geoArea on kit countries-110m): Russia 16.92 M km^2 of 135.02 M km^2 non-Antarctic land = 12.53 points; people 144.82 / 8,161.97 = 1.77 points (population per c1, verified). Over all 16,384 subsets of the other 14 chips, the displayed whole-percent land jump is 12 or 13 and the one-decimal people jump 1.7 or 1.8, so 'about 13' and 'under 2' hold on every path; added ninth after the top 8: land 25% -> 38%, people 53.5% -> 55.3%, matching r6. Recorded only on the first add.

recall.question: Roughly how many countries together hold half of the world's people?
recall.why: India and China alone hold about 35%; adding the USA, Indonesia, Pakistan, Nigeria and Brazil passes half.
